variable.name: GameAchievementBadgeTintVar
variable.description: Dims the badge of an achievement the player hasn't earned. The add-on supplies a separate greyscale badge, but not every achievement has one.

include.name: GameAchievementItem
include.description: Only the focused row scrolls its title and criteria. Scrolling every row at once is unreadable, and the criteria are frequently longer than the column.

control.description: Achievement badge, dimmed while the achievement is locked
Unlock date, shown only for earned achievements
control.label: $INFO[ListItem.Property(achievement.unlockeddate)]

control.description: Progress towards a counting achievement, such as "45/100". Supplied by the add-on rather than built here, because only it knows what is being counted.
control.label: $INFO[ListItem.Property(achievement.measuredprogress)]

control.description: Progress bar for counting achievements. Sits on the rarity line, which is free on the right-hand side, and only ever shows for achievements the player hasn't earned yet.
An indicator that is not showing takes no room, so the rest close up on their own.
Game title and progress. DialogBackgroundCommons draws a static header label, so an empty one is passed above and this scrolling label takes its place for titles too long to fit.
control.label: $INFO[Window.Property(Header)]

control.description: Shown instead of the list to someone without an account: the dialog opens for them so the feature is discoverable, and the code is the shortest route to signing up from the sofa.

Focus fills the whole row so that no text falls outside it. This must be a uniform, stretchable texture. The bordered button textures are shaped for an 80px button, and a border draws its edge strips unstretched, so their transparent margins land at the row's edges and leave the bottom line of text uncovered.
Focusable so that the list can be paged from the keyboard
Leaderboards live behind the achievements they belong to rather than beside them in the OSD. Hidden when signed out, where there is nothing to show and nothing to submit.
control.label: $LOCALIZE[35331]

control.description: Said in place of the list: the boards are fetched when the dialog first opens, and a game may have none at all
control.label: $INFO[Window.Property(Leaderboards.Status)]

control.description: Backdrop, so it stays readable over any game
Badge, where there is one to show
How far along, where that is counted

control.description: Driven by the percentage Kodi sends alongside the text, rather than parsing "13/180" back into numbers.
